reason: The cited evidence confirms BCS-type superconductivity in some HEAs (E3, E5) but does not provide specific data linking d-DOS at EF to Tc in the proposed Ti–V–Cr–Mo–W system, nor does it support the predicted 1–2 K Tc increase or the baseline Tc value for this uncharacterized alloy.
premises: Superconductivity in bcc HEAs is BCS-type phonon-mediated
Tc is governed by the density of d-electron states at the Fermi level
Elements like Ti and Mo have pronounced d-DOS peaks near EF that enhance electron–phonon coupling
A small compositional change that increases d-DOS at EF will raise Tc by 1–2 K
The baseline equimolar Ti–V–Cr–Mo–W alloy will have a Tc similar to Nb–Ta matrix HEAs (~7.5 K)
